Reading a tab moves the column forward to the next multiple of 4 plus 1, so a tab in column 1 lands on column 5 and a tab in column 6 lands on column 9. Every other code point moves the column forward by 1. A token's position is where its first code point sits.

An identifier starts with a letter or `_` and continues with letters, digits and `_`; it is a `keyword` when it is exactly `let`, `if`, `else`, `while`, `return`, `true`, `false` or `null`, and an `ident` otherwise. A `number` starts with a digit. `0x` or `0X` introduces hexadecimal digits, `0b` or `0B` binary, and `0o` or `0O` octal; anything else is decimal digits, optionally a `.` and more digits, and optionally `e` or `E`, an optional `+` or `-`, and more digits. A number followed immediately by a letter, a digit or `_` that the rules above did not consume, and a prefix with no digit after it, are both errors, and the reported text is everything the scanner ran through, up to and including those trailing characters.

You implement one program task in the workspace you are given, against its own test suite, and you stop when the tests pass.

The workspace is your working directory: every bash command and every file path resolves inside it, so read and edit its files by their relative paths and never search outside it.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

## Summary

I implemented the tokenizer in `src/cli.js` (CLI wiring) and `src/lexer.js` (the actual scanner), following the spec closely:

- **Position tracking**: a `Scanner` class walks the input by Unicode code point (handling surrogate pairs), tracking 1-based line/column with LF resetting to column 1 and TAB advancing to the next multiple of 4 plus 1.
- **Whitespace/comments**: space/tab/CR/LF are skipped; `//` runs to EOL/EOF; `/* */` nests with depth tracking, reporting `unterminated block comment` at the outermost opener.
- **Identifiers/keywords**: `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, classified against the fixed keyword set.
- **Numbers**: handles `0x`/`0b`/`0o` prefixes (each with its own digit alphabet), decimal with optional fractional part (only consumed if a digit follows the `.`) and optional exponent (only consumed if a digit, or sign+digit, follows `e`/`E`); single `_` allowed only between two digits of the same run. Both "prefix with no digit" and "invalid trailing letter/digit/underscore" errors report the full consumed text including greedily-consumed trailing characters.
- **Strings**: decode `\n \t \r \\ \" \0 \xHH \u{H...}` into actual characters, then print via `JSON.stringify` of the decoded value (matches the required "decoded value written as JSON string" body). EOF at any point mid-string reports `unterminated string` at the opening quote; a bare LF reports `newline in string` at its own position; any other escape reports `invalid escape \<char>` at the backslash.
- **Raw strings**: `r"..."`, no escape processing, embedded LFs allowed, unterminated input reports at the `r`.
- **Punctuation**: longest-match-first against the two- and one-character operator lists; anything else is `unexpected character`.
- **CLI**: validates the single mode argument first, reads all of stdin as UTF-8, buffers all output before writing (so a failure never emits partial stdout), and maps `ScanError` to `error: <line>:<col>: <reason>` on exit 2.

All 16 provided tests pass (`node --test test/*.test.js`), and I additionally exercised nested block comments, tab-stop math, `0x`/prefix-without-digit errors, trailing-invalid-character number errors, string/rawstring escapes (including `\x`, `\u{...}`, embedded newlines in raw strings), and multi-char punctuation — all matching the spec's stated behavior. No dependencies were added and `node_modules` does not exist; only files under `src/` were changed.

goal.objective:
`src/cli.js` is the program; how the work is split across other files under `src/` is up to you. It takes exactly one argument, `tokens` or `stats`, reads UTF-8 source text from standard input, and scans it. Exit 0 when the whole input scans.

Positions count from 1. Reading a line feed moves to the next line and sets the column back to 1. Reading a tab moves the column forward to the next multiple of 4 plus 1, so a tab in column 1 lands on column 5 and a tab in column 6 lands on column 9. Every other code point moves the column forward by 1. A token's position is where its first code point sits.

Spaces, tabs, carriage returns and line feeds separate tokens and produce none. `//` starts a comment that runs to the next line feed or to the end of the input. `/*` starts a block comment that ends at the matching `*/` and nests, so `/* a /* b */ c */` is one comment; a block comment that never closes is an error reported at the `/*` that opened the outermost one.

An identifier starts with a letter or `_` and continues with letters, digits and `_`; it is a `keyword` when it is exactly `let`, `if`, `else`, `while`, `return`, `true`, `false` or `null`, and an `ident` otherwise. A `number` starts with a digit. `0x` or `0X` introduces hexadecimal digits, `0b` or `0B` binary, and `0o` or `0O` octal; anything else is decimal digits, optionally a `.` and more digits, and optionally `e` or `E`, an optional `+` or `-`, and more digits. A `.` only continues a number when a digit follows it, and an exponent marker only continues one when a digit, or a sign and then a digit, follows it. A `_` may sit between two digits of the same run and nowhere else. A number followed immediately by a letter, a digit or `_` that the rules above did not consume, and a prefix with no digit after it, are both errors, and the reported text is everything the scanner ran through, up to and including those trailing characters.

A `string` is written between double quotes and carries the escapes `\n`, `\t`, `\r`, `\\`, `\"`, `\0`, `\xHH` with exactly two hexadecimal digits, and `\u{H...}` with at least one hexadecimal digit naming a code point of at most 10FFFF. Any other escape is an error reported at its backslash. A line feed inside a string is an error reported where the line feed sits, and a string the input ends before closing is an error reported at its opening quote. A `rawstring` is written `r"` then any characters, line feeds included, up to the first `"`; it carries no escapes, its position is that of the `r`, and an input that ends before the closing `"` is an `unterminated string` reported at that `r` rather than at the quote after it.

The punctuation, matched longest first, is `==`, `!=`, `<=`, `>=`, `&&`, `||`, `->`, `=>`, `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%`, `=`, `<`, `>`, `!`, `(`, `)`, `{`, `}`, `[`, `]`, `,`, `;` and `.`. Any other character is an error.

`tokens` prints one line per token, `<line>:<column> <kind> <body>`. For a `string` and a `rawstring` the body is the decoded value written as a JSON string, quotes and escapes included; for every other kind it is the source text of the token. `stats` instead prints one line per kind, `<kind> <count>`, for all six kinds `ident`, `keyword`, `number`, `punct`, `rawstring` and `string` in that order, whether or not any token had that kind, and then `total N`.

A failure writes one line to standard error and exits 2, having written nothing to standard output; stop at the first one. The message is `error: usage: cli.js tokens|stats` when the argument is not exactly one of the two mode words, and otherwise `error: <line>:<column>: <reason>` where the reason is one of `unterminated string`, `newline in string`, `unterminated block comment`, `invalid escape \<character>`, `invalid number <text>` and `unexpected character <character>`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root. This task is also judged on inputs you do not see: a validator runs your program on its own held-back cases and compares the exit code and output byte for byte. The visible tests cover the main paths only. Implement the written specification, including every corner it states, rather than the behaviour the visible tests happen to pin down.
